t: Founded by the former herdsman Changamire Dombo I, the Rozvi Empire dominated the Zimbabwean plateau from the late 17th century.
Dombo drove Portuguese traders and settlers from the interior in the 1690s, keeping the gold and ivory trade under African control.
Drought, a shift in coastal demand and Nguni invasions of the Mfecane destroyed the state in the 1830s; its stone ruins and Mwari cult endured.
dyk: The Mwari cult patronised by the Rozvi outlived the empire and helped organise resistance to British South Africa Company rule in 1896-1897.
ev: Changamire Dombo builds a power base in Guruuswa under the Mutapa ruler Mukombwe
Dombo defeats Mutapa and Portuguese forces at the Battle of Maungwe
Rozvi forces destroy the Portuguese settlement at Dambarare and sweep away the interior fairs
The Portuguese fair at Masekesa in Manica falls, shortly before Dombo's death
The rise of Shaka's Zulu kingdom sets off the Mfecane, displacing Nguni groups northwards
Zwangendaba's Ngoni cross the plateau; Nyamazana's forces later kill the reigning Changamire
Mzilikazi's Ndebele occupy the former Rozvi heartland
